activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the chain rule: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{tan}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y)) \\  & ={sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))\cdot \frac{1}{x+y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))\cdot \frac{1}{x+y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(x+y) & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))}{x+y}\cdot (x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(1)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y)) \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))}{x+y}\cdot (x\cdot 0+1) \\  & =\frac{{sec}^{2}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡(x+y))}{x+y}\end{aligned}
$$
